title: Projection of a strict supported class to the fixed residue Cartier arrow
statement: Let l be prime, Y, P¹_Y and its diagonal surface noetherian, l invertible on Y, and fix surface derived localizations. Let D be an ordinary strict reduction, H a root system with roots comparison, xi∈Ext²(D.E(diagonalIntegralSource),H) satisfying FiniteCartierNormalization [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-finite-cartier-normalization], s the ordinary completed supported-source limit isomorphism satisfying SupportedSourceConeNormalization [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-source-cone-normalization], and p a derived Ext presentation satisfying p.Presents xi [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-derived-presentation-equation]. Let c be arbitrary Chern data, r a restriction, k normalized coefficient cones, and e:H≅r.F(lineModule(c)) satisfying the specified roots/lineForget equation [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-coefficients]. For all derived-limit models L₀,L and n≥0 there exists a normalized frame a [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-finite-boundary-frame] such that the supported source composite with completedSupportedUnit and p.arrow equals a.cartierMap(L,cartierResidueReducedPro at n+1) [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-finite-boundary-cartier-map]. This is a supportedBoundaryEquation, not a finiteBoundaryEquation; no Chern normalization of c is assumed. The displayed maps are completedSupportedUnit [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-completed-supported-unit], supportedSourceComparison [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-source-comparison] and coefficientRootTransport [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-coefficient-root-transport], with the derived-limit conventions [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models] and the supplied ExtDerivedPresentation [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-ext-derived-presentation]. The source equation is named supportedFiniteBoundaryCartierEquation [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-supported-finite-boundary-cartier-equation] only to share its categorical interfaces.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient coordinate by k.coefficientForget and the canonical constant finite-ring comparison. The residue-action equation of r proves linearity, and k.coefficient_one fixes one. Take sigma,t from the n-th finite-cycle clause hxi and define the line coordinate as e_n inverse followed by t. FiniteRootNormalization and he give the exact line_roots equation. Project the supported source cone at n. Its integral-generator equation hs and the source normalization in hxi identify the projection with the positive finite quotient. completedSupportedUnit sends one to supported one. Regularity of l on the completed coefficient ring and identification of its actual finite quotient give the derived reduction unit; its adjunction extends this normalized integral equation to the finite coefficient source.

Replace p.arrow by xi using hp and the exact presentation comparisons. Apply the n-th finite-cycle equation from hxi. Its normalized source identifies the source with the finite supported constant and its normalized target, together with he, gives the frame line coordinates. Thus the remaining finite arrow is precisely cartierResidueReducedPro. The exact-cone projection identity identifies its completed coefficient input with k.unitMap followed by L.projection n, for any chosen L.
